lessons.title: Can I Pay by Card?
lessons.situation: At a small shop counter, the customer confirms the total and asks for a receipt.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear the total and the clerk's response to a payment question.
lessons.expectedOutput: Check the total, choose card payment, and request a receipt.
lessons.targetConstruction: 카드로 결제해도 될까요?
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: At a different counter, ask the total and pay by card without reading the script.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 이거 두 개면 얼마예요?
lines.en: How much are these two together?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 모두 만 이천 원이에요.
lines.en: They're twelve thousand won altogether.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 카드로 결제해도 될까요? 영수증도 주세요.
lines.en: Can I pay by card? And may I have a receipt?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 네, 카드 여기 대 주세요. 영수증은 바로 드릴게요.
lines.en: Sure, tap your card here. I'll give you the receipt right away.

lessons.title: The Shelf Price Is Different
lessons.situation: The checkout price differs from the shelf label at a neighborhood store.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a discrepancy reported without blaming the clerk.
lessons.expectedOutput: Describe the two prices and ask for a check.
lessons.targetConstruction: 표시된 가격과 계산된 가격이 달라서요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Point to a price label and explain a different amount at checkout.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 저기 진열대에는 팔천 원이라고 적혀 있었는데, 여기서는 만 원으로 나오네요.
lines.en: The shelf said eight thousand won, but it's coming up as ten thousand here.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 아, 가격표가 다른가요? 제가 한번 확인해 볼게요.
lines.en: Oh, is the label different? Let me check.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 네, 급한 건 아니에요. 어떤 가격이 맞는지만 알려 주세요.
lines.en: No rush. Just let me know which price is correct.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 확인해 보니 진열대 가격이 맞네요. 계산 금액을 고쳐 드릴게요.
lines.en: I checked, and the shelf price is correct. I'll adjust the total.

lessons.title: Comparing Two Payment Options
lessons.situation: A customer wants to know whether two payment methods change the final price.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a qualified answer and compare options before choosing.
lessons.expectedOutput: Ask about the final amount and state a reasoned choice.
lessons.targetConstruction: 최종 금액이 달라지는지 먼저 확인하고 싶어요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Ask a clerk to compare two accepted payment methods without assuming either is cheaper.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 카드와 현금 중 어떤 방식으로 내느냐에 따라 최종 금액이 달라지나요?
lines.en: Does the final amount change depending on whether I pay by card or cash?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 아니요, 가격은 같아요. 다만 카드로 결제하시면 영수증을 바로 보내 드릴 수 있어요.
lines.en: No, the price is the same. With a card, though, I can send you the receipt right away.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 그렇다면 카드로 할게요. 나중에 확인할 수 있게 영수증을 부탁드립니다.
lines.en: Then I'll pay by card. Please send the receipt so I can check it later.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 네, 결제 후에 받은 내역을 같이 확인해 드릴게요.
lines.en: Of course. We can check the receipt together after payment.

lessons.title: Explaining a Price Difference
lessons.situation: Two store workers decide how to explain a shelf-label mismatch to a customer.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a precise explanation that separates the display error from the customer's choice.
lessons.expectedOutput: Acknowledge the mismatch, explain what was checked, and offer a clear next step.
lessons.targetConstruction: 확인된 사실과 선택 가능한 방법을 구분해 말씀드려요.
lessons.variation: 가격표를 바로잡되, 이번 결제는 어떻게 처리할지 안내해요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Explain a display-price mismatch to a customer without making an unverified promise.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 진열대 가격표와 계산대 금액이 다른데, 아직 어느 쪽이 잘못된 건지 확인 전이에요.
lines.en: The shelf label and checkout amount differ, but we haven't confirmed which one is wrong yet.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 그럼 먼저 차이가 있다는 점을 인정하고, 확인하는 동안 잠시 기다려 주실 수 있는지 여쭤봐요.
lines.en: Then let's acknowledge the difference and ask if the customer can wait while we check.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 확인 결과가 나오면 이유를 짧게 설명하고, 고객이 계속 구매할지 선택할 수 있게 안내할게요.
lines.en: Once we know, I'll briefly explain why and let the customer decide whether to buy it.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 좋아요. 확인되지 않은 할인이나 환불을 먼저 약속하지만 않으면 되겠네요.
lines.en: Good. We just shouldn't promise a discount or refund before it's been confirmed.

lessons.title: Repairing a Misleading Impression
lessons.situation: A store manager and clerk discuss how to repair a misleading impression about a price label.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear how two colleagues distinguish intent, impact, and an appropriate response.
lessons.expectedOutput: Acknowledge the customer's reasonable interpretation without implying deliberate deception.
lessons.targetConstruction: 의도와 별개로 그렇게 받아들이실 만했다는 점을 인정해요.
lessons.variation: 고객이 어떤 가격을 기대했는지 먼저 확인해요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: A customer says the label led them to expect a lower price. Respond with nuance and a concrete verification step.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 고객님께서는 표시된 금액을 보고 구매를 결정하셨으니, 뒤늦게 다른 금액을 들으면 속았다고 느끼실 수도 있겠어요.
lines.en: The customer decided based on the displayed price, so hearing a different amount at checkout could understandably feel misleading.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 맞아요. 고의가 아니었다는 설명부터 하면 그 경험을 가볍게 여기는 것처럼 들릴 수 있어요.
lines.en: Yes. Leading with 'it wasn't intentional' may sound like we're dismissing their experience.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 우선 혼란을 드린 점을 인정하고, 실제 적용되는 금액과 그 근거를 확인해서 말씀드릴게요.
lines.en: I'll first acknowledge the confusion, then verify the applicable amount and explain its basis.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 그다음 구매를 계속하실지 선택하실 수 있도록 안내하고, 가격표도 바로 점검하죠.
lines.en: Then let them choose whether to proceed, and we'll check the label promptly.

lessons.title: I Booked for Three
lessons.situation: A customer arrives at a salon for a named appointment.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear the receptionist ask for a name and time.
lessons.expectedOutput: Give the booking time and name, then follow the check-in instruction.
lessons.targetConstruction: 세 시에 예약했어요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Arrive for your own appointment and state your name and time without looking.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 안녕하세요. 세 시에 예약했어요.
lines.en: Hello. I have an appointment at three.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 네, 성함이 어떻게 되세요?
lines.en: Certainly. May I have your name?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 마리아예요. 조금 일찍 왔어요.
lines.en: It's Maria. I came a little early.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 확인됐어요. 여기 앉아서 잠깐 기다려 주세요.
lines.en: I've found your booking. Please take a seat and wait a moment.

lessons.title: I Can't Find the Booking
lessons.situation: A salon receptionist cannot find a customer's reservation at first.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a simple booking problem and a cooperative search for details.
lessons.expectedOutput: Explain how the reservation was made and offer a detail to check.
lessons.targetConstruction: 어제 전화로 예약했는데, 한번 더 확인해 주시겠어요?
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: The desk cannot find your booking. Give one detail that may help them locate it.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 어제 전화로 세 시 예약을 했는데, 제 이름이 안 보이나요?
lines.en: I booked for three by phone yesterday. Is my name not showing up?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 지금 목록에는 없네요. 혹시 예약하신 전화번호를 알려 주시겠어요?
lines.en: It's not on this list. Could you give me the phone number you booked with?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 네, 전화번호 끝 네 자리가 사칠이일이에요. 그 번호로 다시 확인해 주세요.
lines.en: Yes, the last four digits of my number are four-seven-two-one. Please check with that number.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 아, 다른 이름으로 저장돼 있었네요. 예약 확인됐습니다.
lines.en: Ah, it was saved under a different name. I've found the booking.

lessons.title: Moving an Appointment
lessons.situation: A customer needs to move a salon appointment and compare two available times.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a courteous request and two alternatives.
lessons.expectedOutput: Explain a scheduling conflict and select a workable time.
lessons.targetConstruction: 시간을 옮길 수 있다면 가능한 시간을 알려 주세요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Ask to move an appointment, compare two offers, and confirm one.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 세 시 예약이 있는데 일정이 겹쳤어요. 오늘 안에서 시간을 옮길 수 있을까요?
lines.en: I have a booking at three, but something has come up. Could I move it to another time today?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 네 시 반이나 여섯 시가 가능한데, 어느 쪽이 더 편하세요?
lines.en: We have four thirty or six. Which works better for you?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 네 시 반은 조금 빠듯할 것 같아서 여섯 시로 부탁드릴게요.
lines.en: Four thirty would be a bit tight, so six would be better.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 좋아요. 오늘 여섯 시로 변경했고, 확인 문자 보내 드릴게요.
lines.en: All set. I've moved it to six today, and I'll send a confirmation text.

lessons.title: Clarifying a Double Booking
lessons.situation: A salon manager and receptionist handle two bookings assigned to the same slot.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear coworkers separate verified booking details from an unconfirmed explanation.
lessons.expectedOutput: State the overlap precisely and offer real alternatives without blaming either customer.
lessons.targetConstruction: 확인된 예약은 그대로 말씀드리고, 가능한 대안을 먼저 제시해요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Tell one affected customer about an overlap and offer a verified next step.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 같은 시간에 예약이 두 건 들어와 있는데, 어느 단계에서 겹쳤는지는 아직 확인되지 않았어요.
lines.en: We have two bookings for the same time, but we haven't found where the overlap happened.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 원인을 단정하지 말고 두 분의 확인 문자를 먼저 대조해 봅시다.
lines.en: Let's not assume a cause. First compare both confirmation texts.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 확인된 내용은 그대로 설명하고, 실제로 가능한 시간만 선택지로 제시할게요.
lines.en: I'll explain what we've confirmed and offer only times we can actually accommodate.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 좋아요. 기다리시게 될 분께는 예상 시간을 분명히 말씀드리는 것도 잊지 마세요.
lines.en: Good. Don't forget to give the person who may have to wait a clear time estimate.

lessons.title: Acknowledge Without Deflecting
lessons.situation: Two salon coworkers refine an explanation after a customer made plans around a confirmed booking.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a nuanced distinction between an accidental overlap and the inconvenience it caused.
lessons.expectedOutput: Acknowledge the disruption without prematurely assigning blame, then offer choices.
lessons.targetConstruction: 실수가 어디서 시작됐는지와 별개로 불편을 드린 점은 인정해요.
lessons.variation: 고객이 이미 시간을 비워 두셨다는 점을 먼저 고려해요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Respond to a customer who arranged their day around a confirmed booking that cannot be honored as planned.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 고객님은 확인 문자까지 받으셨는데, 이제 와서 예약이 겹쳤다고 하면 시간을 허비한 기분이 드실 거예요.
lines.en: The customer received a confirmation, so learning only now that the slot overlaps may feel like we wasted their time.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 맞아요. 누구의 입력 실수인지 따지기 전에, 그 일정에 맞춰 오셨다는 사실부터 인정해야죠.
lines.en: Exactly. Before sorting out whose entry caused it, we should acknowledge that they came in on the strength of that booking.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 현재 가능한 시간과 기다리셔야 하는 시간을 각각 분명히 말씀드리고, 결정은 고객님께 맡기겠습니다.
lines.en: I'll clearly explain the available slots and likely wait for each, then leave the decision to the customer.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 그렇게 하세요. 설명은 짧고 정확하게 하고, 이후에 예약 기록도 따로 점검합시다.
lines.en: Please do. Keep the explanation concise and accurate, then we'll review the booking record separately.

lessons.title: My Stomach Has Hurt Since Yesterday
lessons.situation: A patient describes a stomachache at a clinic; the lesson gives no medical advice.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a clinician ask when a symptom began.
lessons.expectedOutput: Say where it hurts and when it started.
lessons.targetConstruction: 어제부터 배가 아파요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Point to a different body part and say when the discomfort began.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 어디가 불편하세요?
lines.en: What is bothering you?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 어제부터 배가 아파요.
lines.en: My stomach has hurt since yesterday.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 계속 아프세요, 아니면 가끔 아프세요?
lines.en: Does it hurt all the time, or only sometimes?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 가끔 아파요. 특히 밥을 먹고 나서요.
lines.en: Sometimes. Especially after I eat.

lessons.title: Explaining the Symptom Pattern
lessons.situation: A patient describes a symptom pattern so a clinician can ask a relevant follow-up.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear onset, frequency, and a correction to a possible misunderstanding.
lessons.expectedOutput: Describe when the symptom occurs and clarify what does not happen.
lessons.targetConstruction: 먹고 나면 아픈데, 먹기 전에는 괜찮아요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Describe a symptom timeline and correct one misunderstood detail.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 언제부터 불편했고, 주로 언제 아프세요?
lines.en: When did it start, and when does it usually hurt?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 그저께부터요. 먹고 나면 배가 아픈데, 먹기 전에는 괜찮아요.
lines.en: Since the day before yesterday. My stomach hurts after meals, but it's fine before I eat.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 그러면 하루 종일 아픈 건 아니군요?
lines.en: So it doesn't hurt all day?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 네, 계속 아픈 건 아니고 하루에 두세 번 그래요.
lines.en: Right, not constantly. It happens two or three times a day.

lessons.title: Clarifying What Changed
lessons.situation: A patient compares current and earlier symptoms without diagnosing themselves.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a distinction between increased frequency and unchanged intensity.
lessons.expectedOutput: Make the distinction and ask what further information would be useful.
lessons.targetConstruction: 통증이 심해졌다기보다 빈도가 늘었어요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Explain one symptom change precisely, separating frequency from severity.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 지난번보다 증상이 더 심해졌다고 느끼세요?
lines.en: Does it feel worse than last time?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 통증 자체가 더 심해졌다기보다, 아픈 횟수가 늘었어요.
lines.en: It's not that the pain is stronger; it happens more often.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 강도는 비슷하지만 빈도가 달라졌다는 말씀이시군요. 언제부터 그랬는지도 기억나세요?
lines.en: So the intensity is similar, but the frequency has changed. Do you remember when that started?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 지난주 중반부터요. 기억나는 내용을 더 말씀드릴게요.
lines.en: Around the middle of last week. I can tell you what else I remember.

lessons.title: Giving a Precise Timeline
lessons.situation: A patient prepares a concise symptom account for a clinical conversation.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear the difference between observed events and possible explanations.
lessons.expectedOutput: Give a chronological account while separating facts from guesses.
lessons.targetConstruction: 확실한 변화와 제 추측을 구분해서 말씀드릴게요.
lessons.variation: 처음엔 가끔 그랬는데 지금은 더 자주 그래요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Tell a clinician what changed, when, and which part is only your suspicion.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 처음 시작됐을 때부터 지금까지 어떤 변화가 있었는지 순서대로 말씀해 주세요.
lines.en: Please walk me through how it changed from the beginning until now.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 처음에는 저녁 식사 후에만 불편했는데, 이번 주부터는 점심을 먹은 뒤에도 비슷한 느낌이 있어요.
lines.en: At first it only bothered me after dinner, but since this week I've felt something similar after lunch too.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 발생하는 때가 늘었군요. 식사와 관련이 있다고 느끼시는 이유가 더 있나요?
lines.en: So it happens at more times of day. Is there another reason you think it may be related to meals?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 식사와 관련이 있는지는 제 추측이에요. 다만 불편했던 시간을 적어 둔 기록은 보여 드릴 수 있어요.
lines.en: The connection to meals is my guess. I did write down when it happened, and I can show you.

lessons.title: Correcting an Overstatement
lessons.situation: A patient clarifies an imprecise phrase so the clinician does not infer constant pain.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a careful repair of an earlier overstatement.
lessons.expectedOutput: Correct an exaggerated description without downplaying the concern.
lessons.targetConstruction: '항상'이라고 말씀드렸지만, 정확히는 …에 가까워요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: You said 'always' but meant 'often after meals.' Correct the record clearly.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 아까는 늘 아프다고 하셨는데, 통증이 하루 내내 이어진다는 뜻인가요?
lines.en: Earlier you said it always hurts. Do you mean the pain continues all day?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 제가 '늘'이라고 표현했지만 정확히는 식사 후에 자주 불편해진다는 뜻이었어요.
lines.en: I said 'always,' but what I meant is that I often feel uncomfortable after meals.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 그 차이가 중요하네요. 불편할 때는 어느 정도 지속되는지도 말씀해 주실 수 있을까요?
lines.en: That distinction matters. Could you tell me how long the discomfort lasts when it happens?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 시간을 재 보지는 않았어요. 다음에는 시작하고 끝나는 시각을 적어 두겠습니다.
lines.en: I haven't timed it. Next time, I'll note when it begins and ends.

lessons.title: Mobile Data Isn't Working
lessons.situation: A customer shows a phone to a service worker because mobile data is unavailable.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a simple question about whether calls still work.
lessons.expectedOutput: Report the data problem and contrast it with working calls.
lessons.targetConstruction: 전화는 되는데 데이터가 안 돼요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Show a phone and explain which feature works and which does not.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 휴대전화 데이터가 안 돼요.
lines.en: Mobile data isn't working on my phone.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 전화는 걸 수 있어요?
lines.en: Can you still make calls?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 네, 전화는 되는데 인터넷이 안 돼요.
lines.en: Yes, calls work, but I can't get online.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 알겠어요. 화면을 같이 확인해 볼게요.
lines.en: Okay. Let's look at the screen together.

lessons.title: What Have You Tried?
lessons.situation: A customer describes a phone connection problem and one attempted fix.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a sequence of actions and results.
lessons.expectedOutput: Say when the problem started, what you tried, and whether it helped.
lessons.targetConstruction: 다시 켜 봤는데도 달라지지 않았어요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Describe one troubleshooting action and its result to a service worker.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 아침부터 데이터가 안 돼서 휴대전화를 다시 켜 봤어요.
lines.en: Mobile data hasn't worked since this morning, so I restarted my phone.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 다시 켠 뒤에도 똑같았나요?
lines.en: Was it the same after restarting?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 네, 전화는 되는데 인터넷 연결만 안 돼요.
lines.en: Yes. Calls work, but only the internet connection doesn't.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 그렇군요. 그럼 어떤 화면이 뜨는지 먼저 같이 볼게요.
lines.en: I see. Let's first look at the message on your screen together.

lessons.title: Separating Two Connection Problems
lessons.situation: A customer distinguishes a home Wi-Fi problem from a mobile-data problem.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a comparison of two connection contexts.
lessons.expectedOutput: Explain where the failure occurs and ask what can be checked next.
lessons.targetConstruction: 와이파이에서는 되지만 모바일 데이터로는 연결되지 않아요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Compare two network situations without assuming the cause.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 집 와이파이에 연결하면 앱이 열리는데, 밖에서 모바일 데이터로는 열리지 않아요.
lines.en: The app opens on my home Wi-Fi, but not on mobile data when I'm out.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 앱 자체보다는 연결 방식에 따라 달라지는 것 같군요. 다른 앱도 그런가요?
lines.en: It seems to vary with the connection rather than just the app. Does it happen with other apps too?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 네, 다른 앱도 비슷해요. 우선 어떤 설정을 확인해 보면 좋을까요?
lines.en: Yes, other apps behave similarly. Which settings should we check first?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 현재 설정과 표시되는 안내를 함께 살펴본 뒤 다음 방법을 정하죠.
lines.en: Let's look at the current settings and any on-screen message, then decide the next step.

lessons.title: Describing a Reproducible Failure
lessons.situation: A customer gives a service worker enough detail to reproduce a connection failure.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a clear separation between observations and a possible cause.
lessons.expectedOutput: Report the exact conditions and avoid presenting a guess as fact.
lessons.targetConstruction: 원인은 모르지만 이 조건에서는 같은 오류가 반복돼요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Describe a repeatable phone failure: when it happens, what appears, and what remains uncertain.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 원인은 모르겠지만 와이파이를 끄고 모바일 데이터로 전환할 때마다 같은 오류 메시지가 떠요.
lines.en: I don't know the cause, but the same error appears every time I switch from Wi-Fi to mobile data.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 특정 장소에서만 그런지, 다른 곳에서도 재현되는지 확인해 보셨나요?
lines.en: Have you checked whether it happens only in one place or elsewhere too?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 집 근처와 회사 근처에서 모두 그랬어요. 화면을 캡처해 둔 것도 있습니다.
lines.en: It happened near home and near work. I also saved a screenshot.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 좋습니다. 확인된 조건부터 기록하고, 원인은 자료를 본 뒤에 판단하겠습니다.
lines.en: Good. Let's record the confirmed conditions first, then assess the cause after reviewing the evidence.

lessons.title: Avoiding a Premature Diagnosis
lessons.situation: Two support workers reconcile a customer's report with incomplete technical evidence.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear colleagues distinguish an observed failure from a plausible but unproved explanation.
lessons.expectedOutput: Explain uncertainty clearly and choose a useful next check.
lessons.targetConstruction: 그럴 가능성은 있지만 현재 자료만으로는 단정하기 어려워요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: A colleague says the SIM must be broken. Respond without dismissing the idea or declaring it proven.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 와이파이에서는 되니까 유심 문제라고 바로 안내해도 될까요?
lines.en: Since Wi-Fi works, should we tell the customer right away that the SIM is the problem?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 가능성은 있지만 아직 단정하기 어려워요. 연결이 안 되는 조건만 확인된 상태잖아요.
lines.en: It's possible, but it's too early to say. All we've confirmed is when the connection fails.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 그럼 고객에게는 확인된 현상을 먼저 설명하고, 다음 점검으로 원인을 좁혀 보겠다고 말할게요.
lines.en: Then I'll describe what we've confirmed and say the next checks should narrow down the cause.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 좋아요. 추측을 사실처럼 들리게 하지 않으면서도 진행 상황은 분명히 전할 수 있겠네요.
lines.en: Good. That keeps a guess from sounding like a fact while still giving the customer a clear update.

lessons.title: Where Can I Apply?
lessons.situation: A visitor asks where to submit a community-class application; no eligibility rule is asserted.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a direction and confirm the destination.
lessons.expectedOutput: Ask which desk handles an application and check what to bring.
lessons.targetConstruction: 어느 창구에서 신청해요?
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: At a new public-service desk, ask where to apply and repeat the direction back.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 한국어 수업은 어느 창구에서 신청해요?
lines.en: Which desk handles sign-ups for the Korean class?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 저쪽 안내 데스크에서 신청할 수 있어요.
lines.en: You can sign up at the information desk over there.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 저쪽 데스크요? 신청서도 거기 있어요?
lines.en: That desk over there? Do they have the form there too?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 네, 가셔서 필요한 서류를 물어보세요.
lines.en: Yes. Ask them what documents you need when you get there.

lessons.title: I May Have Missed a Form
lessons.situation: A visitor at a class-registration desk learns that their form is incomplete.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear what is missing and ask how to correct it.
lessons.expectedOutput: Explain what was brought and ask for a specific next step.
lessons.targetConstruction: 무엇이 빠졌는지 알려 주시면 다시 작성할게요.
lessons.variation: 제가 준비한 서류를 한번 봐 주시겠어요?
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Your application is incomplete. Ask what is missing and how to fix it.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 수업 신청서를 냈는데, 빠진 부분이 있다고 들었어요.
lines.en: I submitted my class form, but I was told something is missing.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 네, 연락받을 전화번호 칸이 비어 있어요.
lines.en: Yes, the contact-number field is blank.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 아, 그 부분을 놓쳤네요. 지금 적어서 다시 드리면 될까요?
lines.en: Oh, I missed that. May I fill it in and give it back now?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 네, 여기 적어 주시면 바로 확인해 드릴게요.
lines.en: Yes. Write it here, and I'll check it right away.

lessons.title: Confirming the Application Route
lessons.situation: A visitor has seen two possible ways to submit a class application and asks which is current.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a clarification based on the notice at hand, not a universal rule.
lessons.expectedOutput: Compare two routes and confirm the next action.
lessons.targetConstruction: 안내문에는 온라인 접수라고 되어 있는데, 방문해서도 신청할 수 있나요?
lessons.variation: 이 공지에 적힌 방법이 지금도 맞나요?
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Show an application notice and ask whether its stated method is still current.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 제가 본 안내문에는 온라인 신청이라고 되어 있는데, 여기서도 접수할 수 있나요?
lines.en: The notice I saw says to apply online. Can I also submit it here?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 이 수업은 현재 두 방법 모두 가능해요. 다만 신청 내용을 확인하는 방식은 달라요.
lines.en: For this class, both methods are currently available, though confirmation works differently.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 그렇군요. 오늘 여기서 신청하면 접수됐다는 사실을 어떻게 확인할 수 있을까요?
lines.en: I see. If I apply here today, how can I confirm it was received?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 작성하신 내용을 먼저 확인한 뒤, 접수 확인 방법을 안내해 드릴게요.
lines.en: I'll check your form first, then explain how to confirm receipt.

lessons.title: Clarifying an Ambiguous Notice
lessons.situation: A visitor asks staff to clarify whether a posted instruction applies to the current class.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a precise question that separates a general notice from a specific application.
lessons.expectedOutput: Point out the ambiguity and request written confirmation of the relevant route.
lessons.targetConstruction: 이 안내가 이번 수업에도 적용되는지 확인하고 싶습니다.
lessons.variation: 안내문이 갱신된 날짜를 확인해 주실 수 있나요?
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: An old notice and a new desk instruction conflict. Ask which applies to your application.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 게시된 안내에는 방문 접수라고 쓰여 있는데, 이번 수업에도 그대로 적용되는지 확인하고 싶습니다.
lines.en: The posted notice says in-person submission. I'd like to confirm whether that still applies to this class.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 그 안내는 이전 모집 때 사용한 거예요. 이번 모집 내용은 별도 공지에 정리돼 있습니다.
lines.en: That notice is from an earlier intake. The current details are in a separate announcement.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 그렇다면 이번 공지의 링크를 받을 수 있을까요? 제가 다른 내용을 보고 다시 혼동하지 않도록요.
lines.en: Could you send me the link to the current announcement? I'd rather not confuse it with another version.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 네, 최신 공지를 보여 드리고 해당 부분을 함께 확인해 드릴게요.
lines.en: Certainly. I'll show you the latest notice and go through that section with you.

lessons.title: Reconciling Conflicting Guidance
lessons.situation: A visitor received two conflicting instructions about a community-class application.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a nuanced account that avoids accusing either worker while requesting a clear answer.
lessons.expectedOutput: Lay out the conflicting guidance, identify the needed decision, and seek one authoritative confirmation.
lessons.targetConstruction: 두 안내가 서로 달라 어느 절차를 따라야 할지 확인 부탁드립니다.
lessons.variation: 현재 기준을 한 번에 확인할 수 있는 자료가 있을까요?
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Two staff members gave different application instructions. Ask for a reliable resolution without assigning blame.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 전화로는 방문해서 내라고 들었는데, 오늘은 온라인으로만 접수한다고 안내받았습니다. 어느 쪽을 따라야 할지 확인 부탁드립니다.
lines.en: I was told by phone to submit it in person, but today I was told applications are online only. Could you clarify which applies?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 안내가 서로 달라 혼란스러우셨겠어요. 먼저 두 안내가 각각 언제 나온 것인지 확인하겠습니다.
lines.en: Those conflicting instructions must be confusing. Let me first check when each was issued.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 감사합니다. 접수 자체보다도 잘못된 방법을 따라 기회를 놓치지 않는 게 중요해서요.
lines.en: Thank you. What matters most to me is not missing the chance by following the wrong route.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 그 점 이해합니다. 이번 모집에 적용되는 방법을 확인한 뒤, 근거가 되는 공지도 함께 안내해 드릴게요.
lines.en: I understand. I'll confirm the route for this intake and show you the notice it's based on.

lessons.title: This Isn't My Order
lessons.situation: A customer at a café notices the wrong drink at pickup.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a worker ask what was ordered.
lessons.expectedOutput: State the mismatch and request a check.
lessons.targetConstruction: 제가 주문한 음료가 아니에요. 다시 확인해 주세요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: At a pickup counter, identify the wrong item and say what you ordered.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 죄송한데, 이건 제가 주문한 음료가 아니에요.
lines.en: Excuse me, this isn't the drink I ordered.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 어떤 음료를 주문하셨어요?
lines.en: What did you order?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 아이스라테를 주문했어요. 다시 확인해 주실래요?
lines.en: I ordered an iced latte. Could you check again?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 네, 주문 내역을 다시 볼게요.
lines.en: Of course. I'll check the order again.

lessons.title: The Name on the Label Is Wrong
lessons.situation: A café customer sees a similar name on a pickup label and checks before taking the drink.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a polite correction and a specific detail to verify.
lessons.expectedOutput: Explain the name difference and ask the worker to check the order number.
lessons.targetConstruction: 제 이름과 비슷한데 한 글자가 달라서요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Explain a near-match on a label and offer another detail to identify your order.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 이름이 제 것과 비슷한데 한 글자가 달라서요. 제 주문이 맞을까요?
lines.en: The name is almost mine, but one letter is different. Is this my order?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 바로 드리기 전에 확인해 볼게요. 주문 번호를 알려 주시겠어요?
lines.en: I'll check before handing it over. Could you tell me your order number?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 화면에는 삼십이 번이라고 나와 있어요.
lines.en: It says number thirty-two on my screen.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 확인했어요. 이건 다른 분 거고, 고객님 음료는 곧 나와요.
lines.en: I checked. This belongs to someone else; yours will be ready soon.

lessons.title: The Receipt Doesn't Match
lessons.situation: A customer notices a receipt amount that differs from the amount announced at checkout.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a non-accusatory request to compare two amounts.
lessons.expectedOutput: Point out the mismatch and ask what caused it before requesting a correction.
lessons.targetConstruction: 안내받은 금액과 영수증 금액이 달라서 확인하고 싶어요.
lessons.variation: 품목이 하나 더 찍혀 있는 것 같아요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: Show a receipt, compare two amounts, and ask for a check without assuming the cause.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 아까 안내받은 금액과 영수증 금액이 다른데, 함께 확인해 주실 수 있을까요?
lines.en: The amount on my receipt differs from what I was told earlier. Could we check it together?

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 네, 어떤 부분이 다르게 보이세요?
lines.en: Of course. Which part looks different?

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 음료는 두 잔 주문했는데 영수증에는 세 잔으로 표시돼 있어요.
lines.en: I ordered two drinks, but the receipt shows three.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 확인해 보겠습니다. 주문 내역과 결제 내역을 비교해 볼게요.
lines.en: Let me check. I'll compare the order and payment records.

lessons.title: Correcting an Error Without Blame
lessons.situation: Two café workers plan how to respond to a customer's incorrect receipt.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a response that acknowledges the mismatch and states what remains unverified.
lessons.expectedOutput: Explain a careful check and a correction route without guessing at fault.
lessons.targetConstruction: 금액 차이는 확인됐지만 원인은 결제 기록을 봐야 알 수 있어요.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: A customer shows an incorrect receipt. Acknowledge what you know, say what you will check, and avoid assigning blame.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 고객님이 말씀하신 금액 차이는 확인했는데, 왜 그렇게 찍혔는지는 아직 모르겠어요.
lines.en: I can see the difference the customer mentioned, but I don't yet know why it appeared.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 그럼 원인을 짐작해서 설명하기보다 주문 기록과 결제 기록을 나란히 확인합시다.
lines.en: Rather than guessing, let's compare the order and payment records side by side.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 고객님께는 확인 중이라고 말씀드리고, 수정이 필요하면 가능한 방법을 안내할게요.
lines.en: I'll tell the customer we're checking and explain the available correction if one is needed.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 좋아요. 기다리시는 동안 어느 정도 시간이 걸릴지도 알려 드리세요.
lines.en: Good. Also give them an idea of how long the check will take.

lessons.title: Resolving Two Different Accounts
lessons.situation: A café manager handles a disagreement between a customer's memory and the receipt record.
lessons.learnerInput: Hear a way to validate the concern without treating either account as settled fact.
lessons.expectedOutput: Distinguish what each side recalls, identify verifiable evidence, and keep the exchange constructive.
lessons.targetConstruction: 서로 기억이 다른 부분은 기록을 기준으로 함께 확인하겠습니다.
lessons.independentProductionPrompt: A customer and worker remember a payment differently. Respond without accusing either, and propose an evidence-based check.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 고객님은 두 잔만 주문하셨다고 기억하시는데, 제 화면에는 세 잔으로 남아 있어요.
lines.en: The customer recalls ordering only two drinks, but my screen shows three.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 어느 한쪽의 기억이 틀렸다고 서둘러 말하지 말고, 남아 있는 주문 기록부터 함께 살펴보죠.
lines.en: Let's not rush to say either person's memory is wrong. We can review the order record together first.

lines.speaker: Leejin
lines.ko: 고객님께는 서로 다른 부분을 확인하고 있다고 말씀드리고, 기록에 남은 시각을 기준으로 순서를 다시 맞춰 볼게요.
lines.en: I'll tell the customer we're checking the discrepancy and reconstruct the sequence using the recorded times.

lines.speaker: Min-joon
lines.ko: 좋습니다. 확인된 사실이 정리되면 그때 처리 방법을 분명히 안내해 드리세요.
lines.en: Good. Once the facts are clear, explain the next step plainly.
